name: Apache APISIX
summary: A dynamic API gateway that matches requests to upstreams, composes phase-aware plugins, and distributes configuration changes through an etcd-backed control path.

features.name: Dynamic route and upstream matching
features.description: APISIX matches incoming requests against route predicates and applies the selected route's upstream and policy configuration before proxying the request.
benefits: Separates request matching from upstream destination details
Supports many gateway policies without duplicating proxy logic
costs: Overlapping predicates and priorities make route behavior configuration-sensitive
Each route match adds control-plane and data-plane configuration to reason about

features.name: Phase-aware plugin pipeline
features.description: APISIX plugins participate in request-processing phases and can implement cross-cutting behavior such as authentication, traffic control, transformation, and observability around proxying.
benefits: Makes gateway policy reusable across routes
Allows plugin ordering and phase selection to express policy composition
costs: Plugin ordering and shared mutable request context can create interaction effects
Plugin execution consumes request latency and worker resources

features.name: etcd-backed configuration watch
features.description: APISIX stores gateway configuration in etcd and watches configuration changes so gateway workers can use updated routes, upstreams, and plugin settings without a full process restart.
benefits: Provides a centralized configuration source for a gateway cluster
Reduces reload disruption during policy changes
costs: Correctness depends on etcd availability and watch propagation
Operators must reason about configuration convergence across workers

features.name: Upstream proxy boundary
features.description: The gateway terminates or forwards the client-side request at the APISIX boundary and proxies the resulting request to a configured upstream, where retries, load balancing, and response handling affect the observed outcome.
benefits: Centralizes traffic policy and service exposure at one boundary
Allows upstream pools and gateway policy to evolve independently
costs: Adds a network hop and another failure domain
Retry and timeout policy can amplify load or obscure upstream failures

mathematical_views.question: How does a request become an upstream request when route predicates and plugin configuration are selected from a changing gateway configuration?
assumptions: A worker observes a coherent enough snapshot of route, plugin, and upstream configuration for one request
The model abstracts network transport and upstream application semantics
Route matching and plugin phases are treated as an ordered transduction

mathematical_views.question: Which request properties are preserved or transformed when multiple plugins execute across gateway phases?
assumptions: Plugin phase order is the relevant composition order
Plugins communicate through the request and response context exposed by APISIX
The view does not imply that arbitrary plugins commute

mathematical_views.question: How does an etcd configuration update become an effective data-plane configuration across APISIX workers?
assumptions: etcd remains the authoritative configuration source
Watch delivery and worker application eventually converge under healthy conditions
The model leaves update races and transient mixed versions explicit

benefits: Flexible service exposure and policy selection

costs: Plugin interactions add latency and ordering risk

benefits: Fast cluster-wide policy updates without restart
costs: Availability and convergence depend on the configuration path
Extra hop and retry policy can increase failure amplification
